requirement: Converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation: converting an already-upgraded record leaves the file unchanged.

The marked test is `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[loading_is_read_only_and_conversion_is_in_place_idempotent_and_preserves_failures]`. It does the following:
- It writes a legacy record and calls `convert_file` once.
- It asserts that the bytes changed, so the record really was upgraded.
- It calls `convert_file` a second time on the now-upgraded record.
- It asserts that the file bytes equal the post-upgrade bytes.
- It asserts that the file's modification time is unchanged. This rules out a rewrite that produces identical content.

An implementation that rewrites, re-encodes or touches the file on the second call would fail one of these assertions.

I read `convert_file` in `src/evidence_format.rs` to check whether the already-upgraded case depends on the kind of subject. It returns early for any versioned value, after validating it, and the early return is the same for every subject kind. The test therefore needs only the single `Definition` subject it uses. The test does not exercise the other subject kinds, but they are not a separate input class for this obligation. The test also does not run a second pass on a record that was versioned from the start. That path is the same early return, so it is not a distinct case.

The malformed-file and missing-record checks in the same test belong to the atomic and loading requirements, not to this one. The test carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.idempotent`, so there is no marking gap.
